id: mixed-level-root-group-is-not-kazhdan-in-rank-four
kind: claim
title: In rank four the mixed-level root subgroup K_i of EL_4(F_q[x_1..x_d]), d at least two, maps onto E_2(F_q[y]) and has no property (T)
distinct_from:
  mixed-level-root-group-is-kazhdan-in-rank-at-least-five: that is property (T) of K_i for r >= 5; this is the failure at r = 4, where only two full indices remain.
---

**ESTABLISHED.** Let `R_+ = F_q[x_1..x_d]` with `d >= 2`, fix `i`, and let `K_i <= EL_4(R_+)` be generated by
`e_cd(x_i^(eps_cd) R_+)` with `eps_cd = [c = 3] + [d = 2]`. This is the group of
`mixed-level-root-group-is-kazhdan-in-rank-at-least-five`, with `t = x_i` and `r = 4`.

1. `K_i` maps onto `E_2(F_q[y]) = < e_12(F_q[y]), e_21(F_q[y]) >`.
2. `K_i` does not have property (T), and in particular is not Kazhdan for any generating set.
3. For `q = 2`, the abelianization of `K_i` is infinite.

**Consequences for `laurent-vertex-rounds-for-every-model`.**

- The Attempts bullet saying "`K_i` has finite abelianization for `r >= 4`" fails at `r = 4`, `q = 2`. At `r = 4`
  the full-ring part is only the `{1,4}` corner, which is not elementary of rank `>= 2`.
- The property-(T) reduction recorded there applies only for `r >= 5`. The case `r = 4`, `d = 1` is not decided here.
